effects.log: You lead her to an empty hall in your own heavens and tell her it is hers. She stands in the doorway a long time. Then she goes in, and lights a lamp.

events.text: This time the Bride does not fall. She stops, in the middle of the fight, and lowers her hands, and looks at you. 'You have so many rooms,' she says. 'I have been in all of them, I think. Not one was empty. How do you do it?' Her Unborn wait behind her. The fight is over. What comes next is up to you.

choices.text: End it. She is too dangerous to keep

effects.log: You end it. She does not resist. The last thing she says is that your rooms were very warm.

choices.text: Tell her: you fill them. Then let her go and try

effects.log: She goes to try, somewhere far away. You never learn whether she managed it. You hope.

choices.text: Show her how: give her a room, and stay in it with her a while

effects.log: You give her a room and sit in it with her, one evening, with tea. When you go, she stays. She does not go back to the Unborn.

events.text: Thane Ulo is beaten twice, and stands in the shallows of his own tide with his helm in his hands. 'They will know now,' he says. 'The Hollow Dao. It will know I let you.' He does not seem afraid any more, only tired. 'It ate my sea,' he says. 'My coast, my brother, my people. I have served it ever since. I would like to stop.'

choices.text: End him, and let him rest

effects.log: You end it. He goes quietly, like a tide going out, and the shallows where he stood are the colour of a real sea for a moment.

choices.text: Send him away, free, to find his own peace

effects.log: He bows, and goes, alone, into the dark. You hope there is a coast out there somewhere.

choices.text: Ask him to stand with you instead

effects.log: He looks at you for a very long time. Then he turns, and faces the Unborn who were his, and lifts his tide against them.

events.text: The second time, Ulo does not fight to lose: he fights to win, all of it, the whole sea of a dead world behind him, because the Hollow Dao is watching. You beat him anyway. He lies on the shore of {og_passage} and laughs, and the laugh is wet with salt. 'There,' he says. 'Now it cannot say I held back. Now I am free to choose.'

choices.text: Choose for him. End it

effects.log: You end it. He does not argue. The last thing he does is look at the shape of the shore.

choices.text: Let him walk away

effects.log: You let him walk. He goes into the dark alone, and the dark, for once, seems a little afraid of him.

choices.text: Offer him a coast of your own to guard

effects.log: You show him a stretch of shore in your heavens that has no god. He goes down to it, and kneels, and puts his hand in the water.

events.text: Thane Ulo stands with your gods on {og_passage}, in grey armour that has begun, at the edges, to turn the blue of a real sea. When {og_unborn} comes, Ulo goes to meet the commander first. He knows how the Unborn fight because he taught them. He is not kind about it. Afterwards he sits apart from your gods and cleans his blade and does not speak.

choices.text: Sit with him, and do not ask anything

effects.log: You sit with him. After a long time he says the name of his brother. You do not ask anything else.

choices.text: Ask him for the Unborn's weak places

effects.log: He tells you all of them, in order, in a flat voice. The front goes back a good way that season.

events.text: Ulo's tide goes down {og_passage} at your side and the Unborn break on it, and some of them, seeing who it is, stop and stare. They were his once. A few lay down their arms and wait for him. He looks at them, and then at you, and you understand that he is asking a question.

choices.text: Let him take the ones who stopped

effects.log: He takes them. They follow him to his coast and sit on the sand and do not know what to do. He teaches them to fish.

choices.text: Tell him: the war first. The rest after

effects.log: He nods. They fight. After the war you find him on his coast, with the ones who stopped, teaching them anyway.

events.text: The Bride of Empty Rooms does not fight. She walks the halls of your heavens at night, the ones nobody uses, and opens their doors, and lights a lamp in each. In the morning there are gods living in them: wanderers, refugees of dead worlds, small gods who had nowhere. When {og_unborn} comes up {og_passage}, there are many more gods on the walls.

choices.text: Thank her

effects.log: She does not know what to do with thanks. She puts it somewhere carefully, like a cup she is afraid of breaking.

choices.text: Put the new gods on the line

effects.log: They hold. Each of them has a home now, and a god with a home is hard to move. The Heavenly Dao notices.

events.text: When the Unborn open their doors on {og_passage}, the Bride closes them. She knows every door. She goes along the field with her veil back and her face plain and tired, shutting the empty rooms one by one, and behind her the Unborn find themselves standing in the open with nowhere to go. You have never seen her look so close to happy.

choices.text: Follow her along the field, and take it

effects.log: You follow her and take every room of ground she closes. By night the front is a long way off.

choices.text: Leave her to it, and guard her back

effects.log: You guard her back. Nothing gets near her. When she is done she looks round for you, as if to make sure you are still there.

events.text: The front on the Stair of Clouds stands at the last landings. From your hall you can see the Unborn on the marble steps the immortals of the Upper Realm climb to pray. The immortals have stopped climbing. Messengers from the Isles come up anyway, one after another, asking whether the gods are still there. You do not know how many more steps there are to lose.

choices.text: Go to the Stair and hold the landing yourself

ok.log: You take the landing and the two below it. The messengers go home with good news for once.

fail.log: You hold the landing, only just. The messengers go home with a story they will not tell their families.

choices.text: Send word to the Isles: get ready

effects.log: You tell them the truth. The Isles do not panic. They start building, which is better.

events.text: The Unborn stand two steps from the bottom of the Stair of Clouds. If they reach the Upper Realm, the Floating Isles will flood with refugees of dead worlds and with the grey that follows them. The immortals know it. Their sect-masters have sent you, between them, every treasure they own, and a letter that says, simply, 'Please.'

choices.text: Send the treasures back. Hold the Stair for nothing

effects.log: You send them back and hold for nothing. The immortals talk of it for a thousand years. The Heavenly Dao counts it.

choices.text: Spend the treasures and break the front with them

ok.log: You spend every one in a night. In the morning the Unborn are a long way up the Stair, going back.

fail.log: You spend them all and the front does not break. The Stair holds, just. The treasures are gone.

events.text: The front on the Long Well is at the lip. Below, in the mortal world, the sky has started to go wrong: noon too dark, stars by day, the moon the wrong colour. Mortals are kneeling in fields. They do not know your name, most of them. They are praying to whoever is listening. You are listening.

choices.text: Go down to the lip and drive them back

ok.log: You hold the lip of the Well all night. Below, the moon comes back the right colour by dawn.

fail.log: You hold, but the sky below stays wrong for a season. The mortals pray harder.

choices.text: Answer the kneeling mortals first, all of them

effects.log: You give them a sign: a single right-coloured star at noon. They stand up. It is enough to keep them standing.

events.text: The Unborn are in the throat of the Long Well, so close to the mortal world that you can hear its markets. A child's kite has come up the Well on a wind and caught on the Unborn line, and they are looking at it, puzzled. One more push and they will be among the people who flew it.

choices.text: Push them back before the next wind

ok.log: You push them up the Well and out of it. The kite comes free and blows back down to its owner.

fail.log: You push and they hold and the kite is lost in the grey. You hold the throat, barely.

choices.text: Seal the throat with your own body and wait

effects.log: You lie across the throat like a stone. They cannot pass you. The Heavenly Dao counts every hour you lie there.

events.text: The front on the Maker's Thread is nearly at the bottom, where the world your soul made lies small and bright like a lamp in a window. Its own little gods have fled up to you. They stand in your hall, too many for it, asking what to do. You made that world, once. You are its oldest god.

choices.text: Go down the Thread and fight at the bottom

ok.log: You fight at the very foot of the Thread. The little world never knows how near it came.

fail.log: You fight and you hold, but its sky goes grey for a while, and its people notice.

choices.text: Calm the little gods, and send them back to guard their temples

effects.log: They go back, braver. Their faithful never see them afraid. That matters more than you knew.

events.text: The Thread hums like a plucked string under the weight of the Unborn on it, and the world at its foot hums too. In that world, you are told, the faithful say their oldest god is coming back. They are building you a temple, in a hurry, out of whatever they have. You have not been back in a very long time.

choices.text: Go back: stand on the Thread above their temple

ok.log: You hold the Thread above the half-built temple. They finish it, under your feet, not knowing.

fail.log: You hold it, but the Thread is frayed now, and you will feel it fray for years.

choices.text: Send them your blessing, and hold from above

effects.log: You bless the temple from the top of the Thread. It is enough for the faithful. The Heavenly Dao counts the holding.

events.text: The Stair of Clouds breaks. You feel it as a god feels a domain lost, a tooth gone from the jaw of the heavens. Through the break the Unborn pour down into the Upper Realm, and behind them, in a grey flood, the refugees of dead worlds they have driven before them. The Floating Isles will never be quite the same.

choices.text: Go down after them, into the Isles

effects.log: You go down. You are a god among immortals again, fighting in the streets of the Isles. It is a long and terrible year.

choices.text: Stay above and build a new wall

effects.log: You stay and build. It is the right thing. It feels like the wrong one.

events.text: The last step of the Stair of Clouds goes with a sound like a great bell cracking. Immortals on the Isles look up and see the sky above them full of grey, and in it, very far off, a figure under a torn white parasol walking down. Your heavens are still standing. Theirs are not, for a while.

choices.text: Send every refugee god you can spare to the Isles

effects.log: You send them. They know what it is to lose a world. They are very good at helping others not to.

choices.text: Swear that the Stair will stand again

effects.log: You swear it in front of the Heavenly Dao. Oaths in that place are not made lightly. You meant it.

events.text: The Stair breaks while you are fighting on it, and for a moment you are falling with it, among the pieces, toward the Upper Realm. You catch yourself. Below you the Isles are lit up like a festival, and you realise that the lights are fires, and that the festival is a flood of refugees landing everywhere at once.

choices.text: Land among them and help

effects.log: You land in the middle of it and start pulling people out of the grey. Nobody recognises you as a god. It does not matter.

choices.text: Climb back up and keep fighting the rest

effects.log: You climb. The fight is above, not below. It is the hardest climb of your life.

events.text: The Long Well breaks. In the mortal world below, the sky goes wrong and stays wrong: a grey seam across the blue that does not close at sunset. Mortals point at it. Mortals will point at it for a hundred generations. Something has come down through it, and it is in the world now, and you are up here.

choices.text: Go down the Well, though it is broken

effects.log: You go down the broken Well. It is like climbing down a wound. At the bottom the mortals look up at a god with grey dust on their robes.

choices.text: Watch over the mortals from above, and send help

effects.log: You send what help a god can send from the sky. It is not nearly enough. You send it anyway.

events.text: When the Well breaks you hear it below as much as feel it above: the temples of the mortal world ringing their bells, all at once, all through one night. By morning the grey seam is in their sky. They will tell stories about it, and get them wrong, and the wrongness will become what they believe. You cannot stop them. You can only be in the stories too.

choices.text: Give them a sign, so the stories have hope in them

effects.log: You put a single bright star by the seam. The mortals call it the god's lamp. They are not wrong.

choices.text: Listen to every bell, and remember each temple

effects.log: You listen all night and learn every bell. You will come back to every one of them.

events.text: The Long Well goes, and something comes down it into the mortal world: not the whole army, only a few of the Unborn, but a few is enough. The mortals have nothing that can touch them. Their greatest masters are children to an outer god. Below, you can feel the grey moving through the world like damp through a wall.

choices.text: Go down and hunt the few yourself

effects.log: You hunt them down one by one through the world of mortals. It takes years. You are not seen. Mostly.

choices.text: Bless the greatest of the mortals so they can hold

effects.log: You give the mortals a little of your strength. They hold. Some of them become legends. None of them know why.

events.text: The Maker's Thread snaps. You made that world, long ago, in another life; now the Unborn are in it. You feel them land like stones in a pond. Its little gods are fighting in its sky. Its people, who have never heard of the Hollow Dao, look up and see their heaven full of grey, and pray to their oldest god. You.

choices.text: Go down the broken Thread to them

effects.log: You go down the frayed end of the Thread into the world you made. Its people see you come. It is the first time in a long time.

choices.text: Hold the frayed end, so no more come through

effects.log: You hold the end of the Thread in both hands like a rope over a cliff. Nothing more comes down. What is down there already, you will deal with.

events.text: The Thread breaks, and the world your soul made, which was small and bright, goes dim at the edges like a lamp low on oil. Its heaven is full of the Unborn. Its gods, the ones you appointed, are falling back to its mountains. You remember making those mountains. You remember being proud of them.

choices.text: Go and stand on those mountains

effects.log: You stand on them. They remember you, as mountains do. The Unborn do not come near them.

choices.text: Promise the little world it will be mended

effects.log: You promise. The promise goes down the broken Thread like a small light. Its people see it, and hope.

events.text: When the Thread goes, the gods of the world you made send you a message. It is short, and in the old language you taught them, the one nobody else speaks. It says: 'We will hold the mountains. Do not worry about us. Mend the Thread.' They are not strong. They are holding anyway.

choices.text: Do as they ask: mend the Thread

effects.log: You start mending the Thread that same night. It will take time. They will have to hold.

choices.text: Go down anyway. They are yours

effects.log: You go down. They are cross with you for coming. They are also very glad.

events.text: The Stair of Clouds stands again. You built it back step by step, with gods and immortals carrying the marble together, and the last step goes in on a clear morning while the Isles below ring every bell they have. The grey in the Upper Realm is already fading. A pilgrim climbs the new Stair to pray, a little nervously, and nothing stops them.

choices.text: Climb the new Stair yourself, all the way

effects.log: You climb it from the bottom. It takes a day. Every immortal on the Isles watches you do it.

choices.text: Put a ward on every step this time

effects.log: You ward them all. It costs a century of work. It will not break the same way twice.

events.text: The Long Well is sealed again, and in the mortal world below, for the first time in years, the sky closes. The grey seam knits like a healing cut and is gone by sunset, and mortals stand in their fields and stare at a plain blue sky as if they had never seen one. They have never been so glad of nothing.

choices.text: Leave them one star, to remember

effects.log: You leave a single small star where the seam was. Mortals will call it many names. You know which one is right.

choices.text: Go down, unseen, and walk in a market

effects.log: You walk in a mortal market, unseen, under a plain blue sky. It is the best day you have had in years.

events.text: The Maker's Thread is mended, knot by knot, and the world your soul made brightens again at the edges like a lamp trimmed. Its little gods come up the Thread to see you, all together, shy, carrying gifts they made themselves. The gifts are not very good. You keep every one of them.

choices.text: Thank them, and send them home

effects.log: You thank them. They go home proud. The little world is brighter that night than it has ever been.

choices.text: Go down with them, for a while

effects.log: You go down with them and walk the world you made. You have forgotten how much you liked it.

events.text: You become a Dao Ancestor, and on the same day the sky behind the sky opens. It is not a passage. It is the edge of the Hollow Dao itself, a dead dimension's heaven, grey from end to end, and on its plain stand five shapes so large that the six commanders you fought were their errand-runners. The small battlefields were never the war. This is.

choices.text: Walk out onto the grey plain

effects.log: You walk out. The grey is soft underfoot, like ash, like the inside of a closed room. Five heads turn toward you.

choices.text: Look back at your own heavens first

effects.log: You look back. They are bright and loud and arguing. You decide that is worth everything you have.

events.text: The Heavenly Dao of your world speaks to you for the second time in your life. It does not use words. It shows you the grey plain at the end of everything, and five outer Dao Ancestors on it, and behind them the Hollow Dao, which is hungry in a way you had not thought anything could be. Then it shows you yourself, standing in front of it all, alone.

choices.text: Tell the Heavenly Dao you will go

effects.log: You tell it. The weight comes down on you again, the one like being counted, and this time it stays.

choices.text: Ask the Heavenly Dao whether you can win

effects.log: It does not answer. It does not know. That frightens you more than anything else it has shown you.

events.text: The ladder ends at Dao Ancestor; you have reached the top of it. And at the top, where you thought there would be peace, there is a door, and through it a grey plain, and on the plain five outer Dao Ancestors are waiting with the patience of things that have eaten heavens before. One of them, very far off, raises what might be a hand in greeting.

choices.text: Raise a hand back

effects.log: You raise yours. The thing very far off seems pleased. That is the worst part.

choices.text: Shut the door, for now, and prepare

effects.log: You shut it. You will open it again. You spend the next years making very sure you are ready.

events.text: You knew the true battlefield was coming, because the last time you never reached it: the houses fell first. This time you are a Dao Ancestor and the passages still stand, and the door to the grey plain opens on the day you knew it would. Behind you, in the lower realms, {og_houses} are alive and loud. You mean to keep them that way.

choices.text: Walk through without looking back

effects.log: You walk through. You do not need to look back. You know exactly what is there.

choices.text: Look back once, and count them all

effects.log: You look back and count them, every one. Then you go through.

events.text: A soul that has stood on the grey plain before remembers it: once, in another life, you walked here and the Hollow Dao fell. Now it has a new heaven to eat, and the five are on its plain again, as if nothing happened. But something has. You have done this. Some part of the Hollow Dao, you suspect, remembers you too.

choices.text: Walk out as one who has won here

effects.log: You walk out with your back straight. On the plain, for a moment, the five are still.

choices.text: Remember the last time, and do not grow proud

effects.log: You remember how near it was. You are careful. Careful is how you will win.

events.text: The Mouth That Was a Star was a sun once, in the dead dimension, and burned so long it learned to be hungry. Now it is a vast dark ring on the grey plain with a dim glow at its heart. When you come near, your qi begins to leave you, a little with every breath, drawn into the ring like water down a drain. Every exchange with it will cost you more.

choices.text: Fight fast: end it before it drinks you dry

effects.log: You go at it at once, with everything, before your qi is gone. It is a risk of a kind you have never liked.

choices.text: Fight on your body alone, and give it nothing to eat

effects.log: You lock your qi deep and fight it with bare strength. It cannot drink what it cannot reach. It is like fighting with one hand.

events.text: On the grey plain the Mouth opens, and you feel your qi lift off you like steam off a pond in the morning and drift toward it. You have fought gods who were stronger than you. You have never fought one that grew stronger while you breathed. Somewhere in the ring is the dim light of the star it was, and the light is looking at you.

choices.text: Speak to the star inside it

effects.log: You call to the light at its heart. For a moment the drain slows, as if something in there is listening. Then it begins again.

choices.text: Feed it a little on purpose, and watch how it swallows

effects.log: You let it take some qi and watch. It swallows on a rhythm, like a tide. You learn the rhythm.

events.text: The Mouth That Was a Star does not move. It does not need to. You stand before it on the grey plain and every exchange of blows between you costs you qi it keeps, and it keeps it all. The longer you fight, the brighter its dim heart grows, and the brighter it grows, the more it remembers being a sun, and the angrier it is that it is not.

choices.text: Make it remember all the way: show it a real sun

effects.log: You burn as bright as you can, like the sun it was. It flinches. Some hungers can be shamed.

choices.text: Hold back, and make it wait for its meal

effects.log: You give it nothing, and nothing, and nothing. A hungry thing made to wait grows careless.

events.text: The Mirror Without a Face stands on the grey plain like a tall sheet of still water, and in it is you: not your face, which it does not have, but your strongest art, already moving. It has taken the best thing you know before you have used it. Whatever you fight it with, it will fight you with the same, a breath before you.

choices.text: Fight it with your weakest art instead

effects.log: You fight with something you barely know. It copies that. It is very bad at it. So are you. It is an even fight.

choices.text: Show it your strongest art, and look for the flaw

effects.log: It copies it perfectly. Perfectly is the flaw: it does not know why you move as you do. You begin to see where it will go.

events.text: The Mirror does not speak. It shows. It shows you your own greatest art, the one you spent ten thousand years on, moving in its grey surface with no one inside it, and the art is beautiful, and it is aimed at you. You have never seen yourself from the outside. You are, you find, very frightening.

choices.text: Learn from what it shows you

effects.log: You watch your own art from the outside and see three things you have always done wrong. You fix them, there on the plain.

choices.text: Invent something new, now, that it has never seen

effects.log: You make up a move on the spot. It has nothing to copy. For one exchange it is only glass.

events.text: Every god the Mirror has fought is in it somewhere, the way a well holds every face that ever looked down it. When you come near, they all look up. Then they are gone, and there is only your own strongest art in the glass, waiting. The Mirror without a face has a thousand faces, and none of them is its own, and it will use yours.

choices.text: Look for the other gods in it, and call them

effects.log: You call to the gods in the glass. One of them, very faint, moves differently for an instant. The Mirror cracks a hair.

choices.text: Fight it with an art someone else taught you

effects.log: You fight it with the art of a master long dead. It copies it, and something in it falters, as if it recognised the hand.

events.text: The Grey Regent sits on a throne of ash at the edge of the plain and rules nothing, and when you come before it you feel your Dao begin to rot: the understanding you have carried for ages going soft at the edges like fruit left in the sun. It does not hurt. It is worse than hurting. For as long as you fight it, you will be less than you are.

choices.text: Hold your Dao like a lamp in a wind

effects.log: You hold on to it with both hands. It rots slower. You will fight this duel as a lesser god, but not much less.

choices.text: Let it rot. Fight with what is left, and with anger

effects.log: You let it go soft and fight with anger instead. Anger does not rot. It is not wise, either.

events.text: The Grey Regent speaks in a voice like a page turning. It tells you that it ruled a heaven once, as you do, and that it let its Dao rot slowly over a million years without noticing, until one day there was nothing left to rule. 'I only show you,' it says, 'what you are already doing.' Your Dao is going soft as it speaks.

choices.text: Argue with it, and mean every word

effects.log: You argue. You mean it. The arguing is a kind of Dao, and the rot cannot get a grip on it.

choices.text: Say nothing, and look after your Dao

effects.log: You do not answer. You tend your understanding like a garden in a frost while it talks. It talks for a long time.

events.text: On the grey plain the Regent's court stands around its ash throne: the gods of its dead heaven, still bowing, a million years after there was anything to bow to. Their Daos rotted long ago. When you come near, yours starts to go the same way. The Regent waves a grey hand. 'Kneel,' it says. 'It is easier.'

choices.text: Stay standing

effects.log: You stand. It is harder than any duel you have fought. The court looks at you as if you were doing something forbidden.

choices.text: Speak to the bowing court, not to the Regent

effects.log: You tell them their heaven is gone and they may stand up. One of them, very slowly, does.

events.text: The Last Choir is a ring of shapes on the grey plain singing a single long note, and every shape in it is a god it has eaten. Some of them you know. They are gods of your own world, fallen in your own past losses, and their voices make it stronger: for every god you have lost to the Unborn, the note is a little louder, and a little heavier on your heart.

choices.text: Listen for the voices you know

effects.log: You find them in the note, one by one, and say their names. The note wavers where you say them.

choices.text: Sing against it, a note of your own

effects.log: You sing. It is not a very good note. It is yours, and it is alive, and the Choir has none like it.

events.text: The Choir is heavier for every god you have failed to save, and when you stand before it you can feel exactly how many there were: each a voice in the note, each a weight on your shoulders. It is the cruellest thing you have faced. It is not even angry. It only sings, and the song is a list of your losses.

choices.text: Carry the weight, and walk toward it

effects.log: You walk into the song carrying every loss. It is very heavy. You get there.

choices.text: Grieve for them, here, before you fight

effects.log: You stop and grieve for each of them, openly, on the plain. The Choir falters. It did not expect a god to mourn.

events.text: The Last Choir was once the last song of a dead heaven, sung by its gods as their world was eaten. The Hollow Dao kept the song and threw away the world. Now the song eats gods to stay loud, and it is louder for every god of yours it has heard fall. Its note goes through you like cold water.

choices.text: Remember a song of your own world

effects.log: You remember a song a mortal sang below, long ago, about rain. You hold it like a stone in your mouth.

choices.text: Ask the Choir what world it sang for

effects.log: It does not answer in words. For an instant the note changes into something with a tune, and you hear a lost world in it.

events.text: The Hunger Under Heaven is very large and very soft, and it lies at the foot of the grey plain like a fog lying in a valley. It feeds on fear: not yours, but your worshippers'. Every one of them in every world below who is afraid tonight is a mouthful for it, and it heals from every wound you give it while they are afraid.

choices.text: Send word down to your faithful: do not be afraid

effects.log: You send the word. Some of them hear it. The fog thins, a little, at the edges.

choices.text: Fight it anyway, and hit hard

effects.log: You hit it hard. It heals. You hit it harder. It is like fighting the sea.

events.text: When you face the Hunger Under Heaven, below you in the worlds of your faithful the night grows darker, and the dogs bark at nothing, and mothers hold children closer. The Hunger is reaching down to frighten them, so that it can eat their fear and heal. You can feel each frightened prayer go past you into its mouth.

choices.text: Answer the frightened prayers, fast

effects.log: You answer as many as you can, one hand fighting, one hand answering. It is clumsy. It works, a little.

choices.text: Ignore them, and fight it before it is full

effects.log: You ignore them. It is the hardest thing you have done. The Hunger notices, and is curious.

events.text: The Hunger Under Heaven speaks in the voices of your faithful, all of them afraid. 'Help,' it says, in a child's voice, and 'Where are you,' in an old man's, and you know it is only the Hunger and you turn anyway. Every time you turn it heals. It knows how to fight a god: through the people the god loves.

choices.text: Stop turning. Trust your faithful to be brave

effects.log: You stop turning. Somewhere far below, a child is very brave for a whole night. The Hunger goes hungry.

choices.text: Turn every time. You will not ignore them

effects.log: You turn every time. It heals every time. But you are still the god they pray to.

events.text: The Mouth That Was a Star goes out. At its heart, at the end, there is a little star-light left, the last of the sun it was, and it hangs in the grey air in front of you and does not fall. All the qi it took from you comes back in a rush, warm as a summer afternoon. The plain is darker by one ring.

choices.text: Take the star-light with you

effects.log: You take the little light home in your hands. It lives in your hall for a thousand years, and is never hungry.

choices.text: Let the star-light go free

effects.log: You let it go. It drifts off over the grey plain and is gone, and for once something leaves the Hollow Dao alive.

events.text: You beat the Mouth by making it remember. At the end it was burning, really burning, as it had not done since its own heaven died, and it could not drink and burn at once. It chose to burn. It burned out. The plain is lit for a moment like noon in a world nobody remembers, and then it is grey again.

choices.text: Stand in the light while it lasts

effects.log: You stand in it. It is warm. It is the last warm thing in that dead heaven.

choices.text: Go on at once. Four are left

effects.log: You go on. The light fades behind you. You do not look back. Four are left.

events.text: The Mouth That Was a Star breaks like a ring of ice in spring. You stand there, emptied: it took nearly all your qi before the end, and what comes back is slow. You won on your bones. Some of the gods watching from your heavens will tell it as the fight where a god won with nothing in their hands.

choices.text: Rest on the plain before going on

effects.log: You rest. The grey is not restful. Still, the qi comes back, slowly, and you get up.

choices.text: Go on hungry, while the plain is afraid of you

effects.log: You go on with an empty well. The plain does not know you are empty. It is afraid.

events.text: The Mirror Without a Face shatters, and every god it ever copied falls out of it, faint and grey, and stands for a moment on the plain looking around in surprise. Then they fade. Your own art is the last to come out. It hangs in the air, a shape of light, and then comes back to you, and you feel it settle in as if it had been away.

choices.text: Bow to the fading gods

effects.log: You bow to them. Some of them bow back before they go. One, you think, smiles.

choices.text: Gather what you saw in the glass

effects.log: You remember every art you saw in the Mirror. You are a better fighter for having seen yourself.

events.text: You beat the Mirror with a move you had never made before and will never make again. It could not copy a thing that had never existed. For one breath it was only glass, and that was enough. It lies in pieces on the grey plain, each piece showing a little of the sky of your own heavens.

choices.text: Take a piece home

effects.log: You take one piece. It shows your own sky. Sometimes, in it, you see yourself a little more clearly than you would like.

choices.text: Grind the pieces into the plain

effects.log: You grind them to sand. The Hollow Dao will not have this one back.

events.text: The Mirror cracks along a line you made, and in the crack you see, for an instant, what was there before it had no face: a god of reflections, a small one, who once helped lost travellers see the way home. Then the glass falls in. The plain is quieter. Three are left, or two, or one. You have lost count. It does not matter.

choices.text: Remember the small god of reflections

effects.log: You remember it, and later, in your heavens, you set a small mirror by the road for lost travellers.

choices.text: Go on to the next

effects.log: You go on. The plain is wide. You are getting used to it, which is its own danger.

events.text: The Grey Regent's throne falls to ash, and the Regent with it, and the moment it is gone you feel your Dao come back to you, firm, whole, the edges hard again. On the plain its court is still bowing. Then one of them, and another, and another, stands up. They look around them at the grey as if they had just woken.

choices.text: Tell the court they are free

effects.log: You tell them. They do not know what to do with it. They walk off into the grey together, slowly, talking.

choices.text: Feel your Dao come back, and be grateful

effects.log: You stand and let it come back, edge by edge. You will never take your understanding for granted again.

events.text: You beat the Grey Regent by refusing to kneel, which is all it ever asked. When it fell, it said, quite calmly, 'Ah. So that is how.' Its Dao, the one it let rot a million years, goes out of it like dust off an old book. Somewhere under the dust is a little of what it understood before, and you take it up.

choices.text: Keep what it understood once

effects.log: You keep it. It is small, and old, and true. It sits beside your own Dao like a good neighbour.

choices.text: Leave it in the dust. You have your own

effects.log: You leave it. Your own Dao is enough, and it is firm.

events.text: The Regent is beaten and does not fall. It sits on its throne of ash and looks at you, and for the first time in a million years it seems to be thinking. 'I could have stood,' it says. 'All that time. I could have stood.' Then the throne gives way under it and there is only grey, and you, standing.

choices.text: Say: yes. You could have

effects.log: You say it. It is a cruel thing and a kind one. The grey settles.

choices.text: Say nothing, and stand a while longer

effects.log: You stand there a while, for both of you. Then you go on.

events.text: The Last Choir's note breaks, and in the breaking every god it ever ate is set free, a long sigh of voices going up out of the grey like birds out of a field. Some of them are gods of your own world, lost in your own past defeats. They pass you on the way up. One of them touches your shoulder. Then the plain is silent.

choices.text: Call each of them by name as they go

effects.log: You call every name you know. Some of them turn their heads. All of them are smiling.

choices.text: Stand in the silence

effects.log: You stand in the silence where the Choir was. It is the cleanest silence you have ever heard.

events.text: You beat the Last Choir with a song: not a good one, a mortal's song about rain, sung badly on the grey plain at the end of everything. The Choir had nothing to answer it with. It had only the dead. It tried to sing over a living thing, and could not, and went quiet, and fell apart into a thousand small voices that drifted away.

choices.text: Keep singing a little longer

effects.log: You keep singing, badly, for no one. It is the best song ever sung on that plain.

choices.text: Listen to the small voices going

effects.log: You listen. Some of them are humming your rain song as they go.

events.text: The Choir was heavy with every loss of yours, and you carried all of it to the end and set it down. When the note breaks, the weight goes with it. You stand on the grey plain lighter than you have been in a thousand years. The gods you lost are gone, freed, at last. It does not feel like winning. It feels like forgiveness.

choices.text: Accept it

effects.log: You accept it. You did not know you had been waiting for it.

choices.text: Do not accept it yet. There is more to do

effects.log: You put it aside for later. You will accept it when the Hollow Dao is gone.

events.text: The Hunger Under Heaven goes hungry, and lies down on the grey plain like fog in the morning, and thins, and is gone. Far below, in every world of your faithful, the night lifts all at once. Dogs stop barking. Mothers let go of children. Nobody knows why they are not afraid any more. You know.

choices.text: Go down and look at them, unafraid

effects.log: You go down unseen and walk among them. They are not afraid. It is a beautiful thing to see.

choices.text: Go on. The plain is not empty yet

effects.log: You go on. Below you, your faithful sleep well for the first time in years.

events.text: You beat the Hunger by trusting your faithful to be brave, and they were. In a hundred worlds, people who had never heard of the Hunger stood up in the dark and lit a lamp and did not pray to be saved. It starved. You will never be able to thank them, because they will never know. You try anyway.

choices.text: Send each world a good year

effects.log: You send good years down to all of them. They are puzzled by their luck. They deserve it.

choices.text: Remember how brave they were

effects.log: You remember it. Whenever a god tells you mortals are weak, you will remember it.

events.text: The Hunger Under Heaven dies hard. It reaches down into your worlds until the end, trying to frighten them, and you hold its hands back with both of yours until it is too weak to reach. When it is gone you are bruised in places a god does not bruise. But your faithful are safe. The grey plain is almost empty now.

choices.text: Rest your hands

effects.log: You rest them. It takes years. You do not mind.

choices.text: Turn to face what is left

effects.log: You turn. The plain is almost empty. Behind the last grey, something vast is beginning to move.

events.text: The Mouth That Was a Star drinks you nearly dry. You come to yourself at the edge of the grey plain, empty, your qi a puddle where a lake was. It did not bother to finish you. It does not need to: it will wait for you to fill up again, and come back, and be eaten again. That is how it has always fed.

choices.text: Fill up slowly, and learn its rhythm

effects.log: You fill up slowly. While you wait you think about the rhythm of its swallowing, and next time you will know it.

choices.text: Go back before you are full, out of pride

effects.log: You go back too soon. You get away. Just.

events.text: You lost to the Mouth, and the qi it took from you is gone into it for good. You can feel it in there, a little of you, burning in its dim heart. It is a strange thing to be partly inside your enemy. When you face it again it will be a little stronger, and you a little weaker, and it will be a little like fighting yourself.

choices.text: Swear to get it back

effects.log: You swear it on the grey plain. Something in the ring flickers, as if your own qi had heard.

choices.text: Let it go. Fight with what you have

effects.log: You let it go. What you have is enough, or it will have to be.

events.text: The Mirror beats you with your own strongest art, done perfectly, a breath before you, every time. You lie on the grey plain and look up at it, and see yourself in it, standing over yourself, and think: so this is what they felt, all the gods I beat with that. It is not a comfortable thought.

choices.text: Learn humility from it

effects.log: You learn it. It is a lesson you should have learned long ago. Better late.

choices.text: Learn a new art, one it has not seen

effects.log: You go away and make something new. It takes years. The Mirror will not have seen it.

events.text: The Mirror Without a Face wins, and for a moment you see your own face in it, beaten, which is the face it does not have. Then it turns away from you, already copying the next god on the plain, and you are left alone. You were only another reflection to it. That hurts more than the losing.

choices.text: Get up, and be more than a reflection

effects.log: You get up. Next time, you will be something it cannot copy.

choices.text: Watch it copy the next god, and learn

effects.log: You watch. It copies so well. It copies so blindly. You see, at last, where it is blind.

events.text: The Grey Regent wins because you began, without noticing, to kneel. Not with your knees: with your understanding. Your Dao went soft and you let it, a little at a time, and by the end you were fighting as a god much smaller than you are. You leave the plain with your Dao bruised. It will recover. You are not sure you will forget.

choices.text: Tend your Dao back to health

effects.log: You tend it for years like a gardener after a frost. It comes back. Stronger, maybe.

choices.text: Go back angry, before it heals

effects.log: You go back angry. Anger does not rot. You get out alive, and that is all.

events.text: You lose to the Regent and find yourself kneeling at the foot of its ash throne, among its court of gods who knelt a million years ago and never got up. The Regent pats your head with a grey hand, like a child's. 'There,' it says. 'There. Isn't that easier?' It is. That is the most frightening thing of all.

choices.text: Get up. Now

effects.log: You get up. It is harder than anything you have ever done. The court watches you go, envious.

choices.text: Help one of the court up with you

effects.log: You pull the nearest kneeling god up with you, and the two of you walk off the plain together, leaning on each other.

events.text: The Last Choir beats you with your own past: every god you lost sings in it, and in the end there were too many of them, and the note was too heavy, and you went down under it. You lie on the grey plain while it sings over you. Among the voices you hear one you loved once. It is singing against you, and it does not know.

choices.text: Find that voice next time first

effects.log: You promise yourself you will find that voice first next time, and set it free before anything.

choices.text: Get up, and carry the losses differently

effects.log: You get up. You will not carry them as weight. You will carry them as names.

events.text: The Choir was stronger than you because you had lost so much before, and every loss was singing. You walk off the plain beaten and think, for the first time, that it is your own history that beat you. You cannot change what was lost. You can, perhaps, stop it being a song for the Hollow Dao.

choices.text: Go home and mourn properly

effects.log: You go home and mourn every god you lost, properly, as you never had time to. It takes a long time. It makes you lighter.

choices.text: Go back now, heavy as you are

effects.log: You go back heavy. You lose again, but less. The note is quieter.

events.text: The Hunger Under Heaven wins because it was easy to frighten your faithful and hard to stop it. Below, in your worlds, there has been a season of terror without a reason. The Hunger is fat on it, and whole again. You go back to your heavens to find your temples quiet and your faithful hiding.

choices.text: Go down to your temples and be seen

effects.log: You go down and are seen. It is not done, for a god. Your faithful come out of hiding.

choices.text: Find what scared them most, and end it

effects.log: You find the fears it fed on and end them one by one: a sickness, a drought, a bandit band. The Hunger will find less next time.

events.text: You lose to the Hunger because you could not stop turning to the frightened voices of your faithful, and every time you turned, it healed. You would do it again. You know that, walking off the grey plain. It knows it too. It will use it again. You will have to find a way to love your faithful that it cannot eat.

choices.text: Teach your faithful not to be afraid

effects.log: You spend a century teaching your faithful courage: festivals, stories, good harvests. It is the slowest weapon you have ever made.

choices.text: Harden your heart, just for the fight

effects.log: You harden it. It is not a good feeling. It may be what is needed.

events.text: The five are gone, and the grey plain is empty, and then it is not: the whole plain draws in, like a held breath, and what was behind it shows itself. The Hollow Dao has no face. It is the shape a heaven leaves when everything in it has been eaten, a vast room with the lamps out. It turns toward your world. If you lose this, {og_houses} will fall. Houses of earlier lives will stand.

choices.text: Go to meet it, knowing what is at stake

effects.log: You go. You carry the names of {og_houses} with you like a lamp into a dark house.

choices.text: Spend one last day among the living first

effects.log: You spend it below, unseen, among {og_houses}. It is an ordinary day. You remember every minute.

events.text: The Heavenly Dao of your world speaks to you for the last time before the fight, and what it says is a warning. If you fall, the Hollow Dao will take what is newest in this world, what you have built in this life: {og_houses}. What earlier lives built is older and deeper rooted and will stand. What you built now is still soft. It is what will be eaten first.

choices.text: Promise the Heavenly Dao you will not fall

effects.log: You promise. It does not answer. It never makes promises back.

choices.text: Ask whether it is worth the risk

effects.log: It shows you {og_houses}, every one, alive and loud. That is its answer.

events.text: You have walked this far before and lost: you remember it, the way the Hollow Dao came in at the end like night into a house, and how {og_houses} went out one by one, and the long climb back to the morning before. Now it is here again, vast and patient, and you are here again. The difference is that this time you know exactly what it is going to do.

choices.text: Tell it so, before you begin

effects.log: You tell it you have seen this before. For an instant the vast dark is still, as if it had not known that was possible.

choices.text: Say nothing, and use what you know

effects.log: You say nothing. Let it think this is the first time. You know where it will go.

events.text: You feel the Hollow Dao before you see it, as one feels a door open behind one in a warm room: a draught, and the lamps leaning. Then it is there, the whole dead heaven at once. You think of {og_houses}, below, who have no idea. You think of the earlier lives' houses, standing, safe from this. You think of how much one life can build.

choices.text: Fight for this life's houses as hard as for any

effects.log: You will fight for {og_houses} as for anything you ever made. They are no less yours for being new.

choices.text: Steady your Dao, and go in calm

effects.log: You breathe until your Dao is still as a lake. Then you go in.

events.text: The Hollow Dao breaks. It does not die like a god; it ends like a long winter, all at once and then slowly, the grey going out of the plain, the plain going out of the sky, until where the dead heaven stood there is only dark with stars in it, real stars, as though a window had been opened. Your world's Heavenly Dao is whole. {og_houses} stand.

choices.text: Look at the real stars for a while

effects.log: You stand and look at them. Nobody in any heaven has seen those stars before. They are the first thing in that place that is not hungry.

choices.text: Go home at once to your own sky

effects.log: You go home. Your sky is exactly as you left it: loud, bright, arguing. It has never looked so beautiful.

events.text: At the very end the Hollow Dao spoke to you, once, in a voice like an empty house: 'I was a heaven. I was hungry. I am sorry.' You did not know it could be sorry. Then it was gone, and the dead dimension with it, and your Heavenly Dao drew a long breath you could feel in every world. {og_houses} will never know how close they came.

choices.text: Forgive it

effects.log: You forgive it. It is not there to hear. You do it anyway, because you are a god, and you can.

choices.text: Remember it, so that no heaven grows that hungry again

effects.log: You remember. You will tell the young gods about this, and they will not believe you, and that will be good.

events.text: You won. You stand alone on what was the grey plain and the word does not feel large enough. Ten thousand years of the Hollow Dao eating heavens, and it ends here, with you, on an ordinary day. Back in your world, {og_houses} are having an ordinary day too. Somebody is late for dinner. Somebody is laughing. The Heavenly Dao pays you more merit than it has words for.

choices.text: Go and be late for someone's dinner

effects.log: You go down to one of {og_houses}, unseen, and stand at the edge of a dinner, and are not missed, and are very happy.

choices.text: Go to the Hall of Records and write it down

effects.log: You write it down plainly. Who fought, who fell, who won. It is the shortest record in the hall, and the longest.

events.text: You knew how this would end the last time, and it ended badly. This time it ends here: the Hollow Dao breaking like ice in spring, {og_houses} standing in the light, and your memory of the other ending fading like a bad dream at noon. The regression was not a save. It was a second chance, and you have used it.

choices.text: Let the other ending go

effects.log: You let it go. Someone else's grief, now. Then not even that.

choices.text: Keep the other ending, so you never forget the price

effects.log: You keep it, carefully, like a scar. It reminds you what you won.

events.text: The Hollow Dao comes apart in a long quiet, like a great bell's note dying, and behind it there is nothing at all: no more Unborn, no more grey, no more hunger. The six commanders you fought, the five ancestors, the dead heaven they served, all of it gone. You sit down on nothing, a Dao Ancestor at the end of a war, and laugh until you have to stop.

choices.text: Laugh until you have to stop

effects.log: You laugh. It is not very dignified. The Heavenly Dao, you think, approves.

choices.text: Sit quietly, and let it be over

effects.log: You sit. It is over. You say the words aloud, to be sure.

events.text: The Hollow Dao comes in like night into a house, and you cannot hold the door. You feel it reach past you into your world and take what is newest there: {og_houses}, built in this life, still soft at the roots. They fall. The houses of your earlier lives stand, deep-rooted, untouched; the Hollow Dao cannot reach that far back. It is fed, and it leaves.

choices.text: Go down to where they stood

effects.log: You go down. Where {og_houses} stood there are only quiet streets and strangers. Nobody remembers. You do.

choices.text: Go to the oldest houses, and stand among the living

effects.log: You go to the houses of your earlier lives and stand among their people. They are safe. It is not enough. It is something.

events.text: You lost. It is a plain word, and it is the right one. The Hollow Dao is fed, and full, and going, and behind it {og_houses} are gone from the world, every one, as if a hand had wiped a slate. Your older houses, from lives before this one, stand: the warning was true. If your soul can go back, you could fight again. If not, they stay gone, and another life can build anew.

choices.text: Kneel where the last of them stood

effects.log: You kneel. It is a long time before you can stand. When you do, you are already thinking about the morning before.

choices.text: Write their names in the Hall of Records

effects.log: You write every name of {og_houses} in the Hall. Records stay. That much, the Hollow Dao cannot eat.

events.text: At the end the Hollow Dao stands over you like an empty sky and says nothing, because there is nothing in it to speak. It reaches past you. Below, {og_houses} fall, the way lamps go out in a house when the last guest leaves. You hear it happen. The houses of your earlier lives it does not touch: it was never hungry for the old. It was hungry for what you were building now.

choices.text: Remember everything, in case there is a morning before

effects.log: You remember every name, every gate, every voice. If the soul goes back, it will go back knowing.

choices.text: Let yourself grieve

effects.log: You grieve as gods rarely do, openly, for a long time. Nobody tells you to stop.

events.text: You lost twice. That is the thing you cannot stop thinking, walking off what was the grey plain: you knew, and you came back, and it was not enough. {og_houses} are gone again. The older houses stand again. The Hollow Dao is fed again. And still, somewhere in you, a stubborn small voice is asking whether there is a third morning.

choices.text: Listen to the stubborn voice

effects.log: You listen. It is not wise. It is the most like yourself you have felt in a long while.

choices.text: Let it be over

effects.log: You let it be over. Another life can build new houses. That is a kind of hope too.

events.text: The years after the war are very quiet. The passages stand open and ordinary: pilgrims on the Stair of Clouds, prayers coming up the Long Well thick as smoke on a festival night. Young gods who never saw the Unborn complain that the heavens are dull. You let them. You fought a long time so that they could.

choices.text: Tell one of them the story, properly

effects.log: You tell one young god the whole thing. They listen with their mouth open. Then they go and tell it wrong to everyone.

choices.text: Agree that the heavens are dull, and smile

effects.log: You agree. They think you are old and slow. You are, a little. It is wonderful.

events.text: A refugee god of a dead dimension, one of those the Unborn drove before them, comes to your hall with a gift: a little cup made from the clay of a world nobody else remembers. 'There was nowhere left for us,' they say. 'Now there is somewhere.' They mean your heavens. They mean you. You put the cup on the shelf where you will see it every day.

choices.text: Give them a domain of their own

effects.log: You find them a small domain, a valley of rain. They cry when they see it. It is the right kind of crying.

choices.text: Ask them about their world

effects.log: They tell you about it for a whole night. When they leave, a little of that world is still alive, in you.

events.text: There is a new festival in the heavens, though nobody declared it: on the day the Hollow Dao fell, every god lights one lamp for each god lost in the war. The heavens are very bright that night. You light yours last, and alone, and stand among the lamps until morning.

choices.text: Light one extra, for the Unborn who were gods once

effects.log: You light one more. A few gods see it and frown. More of them, later, light one too.

choices.text: Stand among the lamps until morning

effects.log: You stand there until dawn. The lamps burn down. The heavens are still there in the morning.

events.text: Your pantheon gives a feast in your honour, and you sit at the high table and are toasted by gods who argued with you through the whole war, and they mean every word. Halfway through, an old god leans over and says, 'Do you miss it?' and you are horrified to find that you do, a little.

choices.text: Admit it, quietly

effects.log: You admit it. The old god nods. 'So do I,' they say. You raise your cup to that, and to nothing else.

choices.text: Deny it, and enjoy the feast

effects.log: You deny it, and eat well, and dance once. By the end of the night it is true.

events.text: Peace makes the heavens small again: domain disputes, feuds over a mountain's name, a goddess who will not speak to a god about a wedding. You are asked to judge one of these quarrels, and you sit through all of it with perfect seriousness, and give a fair judgement, and go home, and laugh until your servants are worried.

choices.text: Judge every quarrel brought to you this century

effects.log: You judge them all. Small quarrels, fairly judged, are what a peace is made of.

choices.text: Refuse to judge any more. You have earned the rest

effects.log: You refuse, politely. Nobody argues. You go and sit by a lake for fifty years.

events.text: Our Heavenly Dao speaks to you once, the way it spoke to nobody in the war: not a voice, a certainty. The passages are healed. Something must stand where the Hollow Dao stood, at the edge of heaven, so that nothing else hungry finds the way in. It could be you. It would be the end of this life, and the beginning of a watch that does not end.

choices.text: Go to the edge of heaven, and keep it

effects.log: You go out past the last passage and stand where the grey once stood, and our heaven closes gently behind you.

choices.text: Not yet. There is still a life to live

effects.log: The certainty goes quiet, and waits. It is patient. It has learned patience from you.

events.text: You find yourself at the edge of heaven again without meaning to go there, looking out at the dark where a dimension used to be. It is very quiet. You understand that the edge needs a keeper, and that our Heavenly Dao has been waiting, politely, for you to notice.

choices.text: Stay at the edge, for good

effects.log: You sit down on the edge of heaven, and do not get up again. Behind you, every passage sleeps soundly.

choices.text: Go home. Someone else can keep it, or you can, later

effects.log: You walk home slowly. The edge will still be there. So, for now, will you.

events.text: A refugee god of a dead world asks you, very quietly, who will keep the door now. 'In my heaven,' they say, 'there was nobody. That is how the hunger came in.' They do not ask you to do it. They only look at the dark beyond the passages, and then at you.

choices.text: Tell them: you will

effects.log: You go to the door and become it. The refugee god lights a lamp for you every year, for as long as there are years.

choices.text: Tell them: not yet, but it will be kept

effects.log: They nod, and believe you, which is a weight of its own. The door stays open in your mind, waiting.

events.text: A stranger comes to your temple, grey-robed, with a face you cannot hold in memory for more than a moment. They do not pray. They stand at the back and look at you, a long time, as one looks at a house where someone once lived. Your soul remembers before you do: the Unborn. One of them has come to see whether the one who ended the Hollow Dao is back.

choices.text: Turn and face it

ok.log: You turn, and it is gone, in a smell of ash. It knows now that you are back. So do you.

fail.log: It meets your eyes and you are suddenly very tired, as if you had been fighting a long war. Then it is gone.

choices.text: Pretend you have not seen it

effects.log: You pretend. It watches you a while longer, unsure. It goes, uncertain. Uncertain is good.

events.text: Something has been asking questions about you in the halls of the Divine Realm: who you were before, how far back your soul goes, what you did once on a grey plain. The asker is gone by the time you hear of it, but it left ash on a chair. An avatar of the Unborn, sent by what is left of them, sniffing after the soul that ended their heaven.

choices.text: Set a ward where it sat

effects.log: You ward the chair, and the hall, and in the end your whole domain. Nothing grey sits anywhere of yours again.

choices.text: Send word: come and ask me yourself

effects.log: You send the word into the dark. Nothing answers. Something, you are fairly sure, hears.

events.text: On the night of a great gathering, among the guests, there is one who is not anyone's guest. It sits at the end of a long table and does not eat. When you look at it, it lifts a cup to you, and you know that gesture, from another life: Ashkel, or something wearing his manners. It drinks. Then the seat is empty.

choices.text: Cross the hall and catch it before it goes

ok.log: You catch the edge of its grey sleeve. It tears, and you are left holding a scrap of ash, and a note: 'Again.'

fail.log: You cross the hall too slowly. The seat is empty and cold. On the table a cup is still steaming.

choices.text: Lift your own cup back

effects.log: You lift it. Across the hall nobody is there to see it. You drink anyway, to an old enemy.

events.text: A god of your acquaintance comes to you pale and shaking: something followed them home from the edge of the Divine Realm, something that kept asking after you by a name you have not used in this life. It wore their own face, they say, but wrong, like a reflection in a cracked mirror. The Unborn have not forgotten you. They are only smaller now, and patient.

choices.text: Hunt it down yourself

effects.log: You hunt it for a year. When you find it, it is very small, and it runs. You let it run, carrying a message.

choices.text: Calm your friend, and keep them close

effects.log: You keep your friend close for a decade. Nothing comes again. They never quite believe it is gone.

events.text: Your soul has ended a heaven-eater once, and the heavens are full of small grey things that remember it. One of them has been sleeping in a temple of yours, folded small in the rafters, like a moth. It eats nothing. It watches. When you find it, it says, in a gentle old voice, 'Oh. It is you again, dear. I only wanted to see.'

choices.text: Let it see, and then send it away

effects.log: You let it look. It looks a long while. Then it goes, slowly, and does not come back.

choices.text: Drive it out of the temple

ok.log: You drive it out through the roof. It goes with a little cry. The temple is yours again.

fail.log: It is gone before you strike, and three temples have a grey film on their lamps for a month.

events.text: A refugee god comes up out of the dark between worlds, alone, carrying nothing but a kite. Their world had a festival of kites, they say; the Unborn ate it in a season. They are the last one who knows how the kites were made. They ask for nothing. They would like, if it is no trouble, somewhere with wind.

choices.text: Give them a hill in your domain, with wind

effects.log: You give them a hill. In spring the sky over it is full of kites of a world nobody else remembers.

choices.text: Ask them to teach your faithful the kites

effects.log: They teach. Within a generation your faithful fly the dead world's kites at every festival. It is alive again, a little.

events.text: In the quiet years a whisper goes round the heavens: that the Unborn were gods once, of a real heaven, before the Hollow Dao ate it and wore them like gloves. Some gods say it to make the Unborn less frightening. It makes them more. You find you cannot stop thinking about what you would become, if your own heaven were eaten.

choices.text: Ask the refugees of dead worlds if it is true

effects.log: They say it is. They name some of the Unborn as gods they knew. You stop sleeping well for a while.

choices.text: Decide it does not matter: they still come

effects.log: You decide it does not matter. You are not sure you believe it.

events.text: A god who held the passage with you has fallen, in the last field, and their hall stands empty at the edge of the heavens. Their servants do not know what to do. Their faithful below are still praying to them, every day, not knowing. Somebody has to tell them, or answer in their place.

choices.text: Answer their faithful yourself, in their name

effects.log: You answer in their name for a century, until the faithful are ready. They never know. You think the fallen god would approve.

choices.text: Go down and tell the faithful the truth

effects.log: You tell them. They weep, and then they build a shrine, and the shrine has the god's name on it in big letters.

events.text: Your pantheon holds council in the quiet years, and the council is about the war, and the council is a disaster: old grudges, old feuds, a god who will not sit next to another god because of something that happened before the mountains. You sit through all of it. At the end, the eldest asks what you think.

choices.text: Tell them plainly what the passages need

effects.log: You tell them. It is not polite. It is true. Some of them listen.

choices.text: Tell them a story about the last field instead

effects.log: You tell them about an Unborn commander singing a dead sea's song in the dark. Nobody argues for the rest of the council.

events.text: The young gods of your pantheon want to go to the passages, all of them, at once, with banners. They have heard the stories. They think it is glorious. You remember the first time you saw a world eaten, and what it looked like, and how little glory there was in it. They are waiting for you to say yes.

choices.text: Say yes, but take them yourself, and teach them

effects.log: You take them yourself. You teach them to hold a narrow place. Some of them stop thinking it is glorious. All of them come back.

choices.text: Say no. Not yet. Not these ones

effects.log: You say no. They are furious. They will be alive to be furious for a long time.

events.text: A mortal's prayer reaches you in the quiet years, very clear, from a small temple you had nearly forgotten. It does not ask for rain or a son or a good harvest. It asks: 'Are the gods afraid?' You read it four times. You are not sure how to answer a question like that from a mortal.

choices.text: Answer it honestly: yes

effects.log: You send a dream: a god, afraid, standing at a narrow place anyway. The mortal wakes and tells everyone. Your temple fills.

choices.text: Answer it kindly: not of anything you need fear

effects.log: You send a calm dream. The mortal sleeps well. You do not, that night.

events.text: A letter arrives in the quiet years, from Karrow Who Counts: a full and careful accounting of your heavens, everything they hold, valued to the last pebble, with a note at the bottom: 'For your records. I thought you would like to know what you are defending.' It is a very good accounting. You find three things you did not know you had.

choices.text: Use it. Fortify what Karrow valued highest

effects.log: You fortify the three things Karrow valued most. Karrow, you suspect, will notice, and be annoyed.

choices.text: Burn it unread past the first page

effects.log: You burn it. You do not want to know what your world is worth in that ledger.

events.text: Your servants have taken up the war in their own way: they cook as if for an army, every day, against the day the gods come back hungry from a field. The kitchens of your hall smell of bread and broth at all hours. You come in once from the passages and find a feast waiting, and nobody to eat it but you, and you eat it all.

choices.text: Eat it all, and thank them

effects.log: You eat it all. The servants watch you do it, satisfied, as if they had won a battle. They have.

choices.text: Invite the refugee gods to eat with you

effects.log: You send for the refugees of dead worlds. They come shy and stay late. It is the loudest dinner your hall has seen.

events.text: Immortals of the Upper Realm, who have heard of the war, come up the Stair of Clouds in their hundreds to volunteer. They are not gods. They are brave and willing and nowhere near strong enough. They stand in your courtyard with their swords polished and their faces very serious, waiting for you to tell them where to stand.

choices.text: Send them home with honour

effects.log: You send them home with your blessing. They are disappointed. They are alive. Some of them become gods themselves, later.

choices.text: Give them work that is real: carry, watch, heal

effects.log: You give them the work that needs doing. They do it very well. The Heavenly Dao counts every pair of hands.

events.text: A child-god, born of a refugee world, asks you for a story. Not a story about the war; they have heard enough of those. A story about before. You find you have to think a long time to remember a story from before the war, and when you tell it, you are surprised how much it means to you.

choices.text: Tell them about your first life

effects.log: You tell them about a life so long ago you only half remember. They fall asleep halfway, which is the best review a story can get.

choices.text: Ask them to tell you one of theirs

effects.log: They tell you a story from their dead world, about a fox and a river. It is very good. You will remember it.

events.text: The Heavenly Dao pays its merit faithfully, and in the quiet years you sit and look at what you have earned: divine artifacts, pills, techniques no god has ever learned. It is a great deal. It is merit paid for passages held and fields closed. Every piece of it has a battle in it. You are not sure you like how much of it there is.

choices.text: Spend some of it on others

effects.log: You spend it on the gods who held beside you. They are startled. They use it well.

choices.text: Keep it, against the true battlefield

effects.log: You keep it. Something in you knows the small battlefields are not the end of this.

events.text: In the quiet years you dream of grey: a grey plain, a grey sky, a grey room with the lamps out. You wake each time with the feeling of a hand just leaving your shoulder. A heart demon, your servants whisper. But you have fought heart demons. This one does not want anything from you. It only wants to be let in.

choices.text: Face the dream: walk into the grey room

effects.log: You walk into the room in your dream and light a lamp. You wake in tears and the dreams stop.

choices.text: Sleep less, and fight more

effects.log: You sleep less. The dreams wait. They are patient, like everything that comes from there.

events.text: After a field, among the Unborn left on it, you find one that was not quite finished: a small grey shape in the grass, still holding the shape of a god of its own dead world, a little sea-god, you think, from the shell in its hand. It is dying. It does not fight you. It only holds out the shell.

choices.text: Take the shell, and stay until it goes

effects.log: You take the shell. You stay until it goes, which is not long. You bury the grey where it lay, as one buries a god.

choices.text: Carry it to the Unborn side of the field

effects.log: You carry it to the edge of the Unborn side and set it down. In the morning it is gone, and the shell with it.

events.text: An old rival of yours, a god you fought for a domain once and beat, comes to you in the quiet years and asks you to teach them how to hold a passage. They hate asking. You can see it in every line of them. They ask anyway, because they have seen a field, and they know now that it is bigger than either of you.

choices.text: Teach them, as an equal

effects.log: You teach them. By the end you are not rivals any more, quite. You are something you do not have a word for.

choices.text: Teach them, and make them pay in pride

effects.log: You teach them, and make them ask for every lesson. It is petty. It is very satisfying. They learn anyway.

events.text: Your temples below have heard, somehow, of the war in the heavens: not the truth, but a story, in which their god holds a door against the dark. They pray for you now. Not to you; for you. It is a strange thing for a god, to be prayed for. You find it gives you strength you did not know you had been missing.

choices.text: Send them a sign that you have heard

effects.log: You send them a lamp that does not go out. They put it in the temple and bring their children to see it.

choices.text: Keep it secret, and let it be theirs

effects.log: You say nothing. Their prayers are theirs. You only listen, every night.

events.text: In the quiet years a minor god of the heavens takes it upon themselves to make a map of the war: every field, every passage, every commander and where they were last seen. It is very beautiful and almost entirely wrong. They bring it to you to check, nervously, as a student brings an essay.

choices.text: Correct it, kindly, line by line

effects.log: You correct it for a month. At the end it is a good map, and they are a good mapmaker, and you have a friend.

choices.text: Use the map to plan the next field

effects.log: You use it. Wrong as it was, it shows you a way round the next field you had never seen.

events.text: You meet, at a feast, a goddess of the harvest you remember dying: last time, on the Long Well, in the second field. She is laughing about a bad pun. She has no idea. You stand there with a cup in your hand and cannot remember any of the small talk of the heavens, and she asks if you are all right.

choices.text: Tell her to stay away from the Long Well

effects.log: You tell her, oddly, earnestly. She laughs. Then she looks at your face, and stops laughing, and promises.

choices.text: Laugh at the pun

effects.log: You laugh. It is a terrible pun. You laugh a great deal longer than it deserves.

events.text: The quiet years are the worst for one who knows. You remember what is coming; you cannot hurry it; you cannot make anyone else feel it. The other gods are enjoying the peace. You catch yourself resenting them for it, and then you are ashamed, because the peace is what you came back for.

choices.text: Enjoy the peace, on purpose, for a year

effects.log: You make yourself enjoy it. By the end of the year you have nearly learned how.

choices.text: Spend it preparing, alone, again

effects.log: You prepare. Everyone thinks you are strange. You are ready earlier than you were.

events.text: You remember a mistake from the life you lost: a letter you did not send to a god who might have helped. Here is the same god, in the same hall, unaware of either life. You write the letter. It is the shortest letter of your life. It says, 'I will need you later. Will you come?' The answer comes back the same day: 'Yes. Why?'

choices.text: Tell them why

effects.log: You tell them why. They are silent for a long time. Then they come and sit in your hall and ask what to do.

choices.text: Tell them only: you will see

effects.log: You write back: 'You will see.' They come anyway, curious. That is enough.

events.text: Among the gods, the old story is told again in the quiet years: how once, in a life of yours long past, a god walked onto a grey plain and the Hollow Dao fell. They tell it badly and with great relish. They do not know the god in the story is you. You let them tell it, and do not correct the parts they get wrong.

choices.text: Correct one detail, just one

effects.log: You say, mildly, that the god in the story did not laugh at the end. 'Yes, they did,' someone says. 'Everyone knows.' You let it go.

choices.text: Listen, and remember it from the inside

effects.log: You listen and remember it from the inside: how cold, how near. They make it sound easy. It was not.

events.text: A refugee god, very old, comes to your hall and kneels. They were saved, they say, on a grey plain, long ago, by a god who ended a heaven-eater. They have looked for that god's soul through a hundred thousand years. They are sure it is in you. 'I know you do not remember me,' they say. 'I remember you.'

choices.text: Lift them up, and say thank you

effects.log: You lift them up. You do not remember. You thank them anyway, and mean it.

choices.text: Ask what you were like, then

effects.log: They tell you. You were braver than you feel. Kinder, too. You decide to try to live up to it.

events.text: On the far side of the passages, the Unborn have a name for you. You hear it from a refugee who crossed the dark: it means the one who closed the door. They give it to your soul, not to you, and they say it the way mortals say the name of a storm. The quiet years are quieter, perhaps, because of it.

choices.text: Wear the name, and let them hear you wear it

effects.log: You let it be known that you know the name. On the passages the Unborn come more carefully.

choices.text: Refuse the name. This life has its own

effects.log: You will not live in another life's shadow. You will make your own name. You suspect they will give you that one, too.
